sections.heading: When to escalate from PI to cascaded
sections.text: Escalate when: (a) single-loop PI fails overshoot specs at the required bandwidth, (b) the plant has significant current dynamics that a voltage loop cannot handle, (c) current limiting is required for protection. The cascaded structure lets the inner loop handle fast dynamics.

sections.heading: When to escalate from voltage-mode to current-mode
sections.text: Escalate when: (a) the plant has a variable duty-cycle-to-output gain (boost, buck-boost), (b) the plant needs cycle-by-cycle current limiting, (c) the single-loop response is inconsistent across operating points. Current-mode control linearizes the plant.

sections.heading: When to switch topology families
sections.text: Switch when: (a) the RHPZ or other fundamental plant limitation prevents meeting bandwidth specs, (b) the efficiency requirement cannot be met, (c) isolation is required but the current topology is non-isolated, (d) bidirectional power flow is required but the current topology is unidirectional.

sections.heading: When to abandon current-mode control
sections.text: Rare, but consider when: (a) current sensing noise is too high and cannot be filtered without destabilizing the loop, (b) the plant is inherently first-order and current-mode adds complexity without benefit, (c) the application is very low power where sensing overhead is disproportionate.

sections.heading: Topology selection decision tree
sections.text: Vout < Vin? -> Buck family. Vout > Vin? -> Boost family. Both possible? -> Buck-boost or isolated. Need isolation? -> Flyback (<75W), forward (75-200W), half/full bridge (>200W). Need bidirectional? -> DAB. Need AC output? -> Inverter family. Need PFC? -> PFC family. Need three-level? -> NPC or T-type.
